newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian dollar ends firmer in thin trading.
newsitem.headline: Canadian dollar ends firmer in thin trading.

text.p: * The Canadian dollar ended firmer at C$1.3648 (US$0.7327) from this morning's open of C$1.3670 (US$0.7315) after European buying interest buoyed the unit. * Dealers said the currency made some gains against its U.S. counterpart after the big dollar drifted off in the afternoon ahead of Friday's U.S. non-farm payrolls report.
Traders said the U.S. dollar was also under pressure from comments by U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin, who suggested that trade frictions with Japan were brewing.
The Canadian dollar made some gains on continued fears that the timetable for European Monetary Union may be delayed.

Investor confidence in European integration was given a further jolt on Thursday with the release of jobless numbers in Germany showing a rise of 5,000 in February's unemployment to a postwar record of 4.31 million.

On the crosses, Canada eased to 1.2565 marks from Wednesday's close of 1.2572 marks and held steady around 88.62 yen. ((Paul Casciato, Reuters Toronto Bureau 416 941-8100 or email: paul.casciato@reuters.com))
